title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Draft Approval and Pre-Issue Revision Rounds
content:
Every document in the `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` range begins life as a draft. This page covers how quickly the draft is sent, how a draft becomes approved, how long the line waits for the shipper's answer, and how many times an approved draft may be reopened for revision while it is still unissued.

## Sending the draft

The line sends the draft within the tier's draft service standard, a number of hours counted from receipt of the shipping instructions.

## Approval

1. Approval of a draft is an act of the shipper alone; nobody else, including the desk, can approve on the shipper's behalf.
2. If the shipper gives no answer within the tier's deemed-approval period, measured from the moment the draft was sent, the system marks the draft deemed approved. A deemed-approved draft goes to issue in exactly the wording drafted.

## Revision rounds while unissued

3. While a document is unissued, the documentation party may ask for changes to the draft at no charge. The approved draft is returned to draft status, the change is made as a correction, and the revised draft is sent to the shipper for approval once more.
4. A draft may be returned to draft status only while the number of revision rounds already used is lower than the tier's round limit. A revision round is a correction request on the document that has been completed and was registered before the date of issue shown on the document record; for a document whose record shows no date of issue, every completed correction request on it counts. The count is taken from the documentation service requests on the record.
5. When the round limit has been reached, the draft is not reopened again; any further change can only be made after issue, and then at the post-issue correction charges.
6. A revision round before issue never costs anything and is never counted against the cap on corrections after issue.

## Tier values

| Document type | Draft sent within (hours after shipping instructions) | Deemed approval after (hours from draft sent) | Revision rounds before issue (maximum) |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | 12 | 48 | 5 |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | 6 | 48 | 5 |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 12 | 24 | 4 |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | 12 | 24 | 4 |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | 24 | 24 | 4 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | 24 | 24 | 3 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Document type | Completed rounds on record | May the approved draft be reopened? |
|---|---|---|
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 3 | Yes, 3 is lower than 4 |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 4 | No, the limit of 4 is reached |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | 2 | Yes, 2 is lower than 3 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | 3 | No |

## Basis Q&A

**The forwarder, not the shipper, says it approves the draft. Does that count as approval?** No. Only the shipper approves; otherwise the draft stays unapproved until the shipper answers or the deemed-approval period runs out.

**Does a free revision before issue reduce the number of corrections available after issue?** No. Pre-issue rounds and post-issue corrections are counted separately.
